key_insight: Agentic LLM systems can produce breast cancer treatment recommendations, but their quality is inconsistent and not yet reliable enough for unsupervised clinical use.
clinical_relevance: This study shows that adding tools and autonomous agents may help in some cases, but persistent oncology-specific errors and overconfidence remain important safety concerns.
method: Evaluated 7 LLM pipelines, including single-model baselines, tool-augmented systems, and multi-agent setups.
Used 72 real breast cancer cases spanning stages I to IV.
Compared outputs against 1,147 case-specific rubrics generated with AIRG using hidden real clinical decisions.
evidence_signal: The top system, Claude Opus 4.8 with D&C+SA, reached a global score of 0.594 ± 0.025, with performance varying by disease stage and clinical domain.
watch_item: Because the models still showed incorrect or missing recommendations, flawed justifications, citation errors, outdated claims, and overconfidence, they should not be used without strong human oversight.
paper_title: Agentic systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations
